previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old male with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, coronary artery disease, and diabetes was admitted with left-sided chest pain, nausea, and body aches that began two hours after a hemodialysis session. Initial concerns included acute coronary syndrome, but serial cardiac enzymes were normal and EKG changes were stable. The chest pain resolved and did not recur during the hospital stay. Elevated potassium on admission improved with dialysis. A chest X-ray showed new bibasilar opacities, likely atelectasis, with no clinical signs of infection. The patient's symptoms were determined to be non-cardiac, possibly related to dialysis disequilibrium or recent endoscopic procedures. He remained stable, tolerated a light diet, completed a hemodialysis session prior to discharge, and was discharged home in good condition with instructions to continue all home medications and follow up with his specialists.

Brief Hospital Course:
Patient is a ___ yo man with h/o CAD, ESRD, and DM2 who presented 
s/p episode of substernal chest pain and was found to have 
hyperkalemia and bradycardia.
.
# Hyperkalemia:  On arrival to the ED, the patient was found to 
have a K+ of 6.7 and peaked T waves on ECG.  He received 
bicarbonate, insulin with D50, and Kayexalate and was emergently 
dialyzed in the ED.  His K+ decreased to 4.2.  The patient has a 
h/o hyperkalemia in the setting of dietary non-compliance. His 
potassium was monitored and he did not have any other acute 
events during this hospitalization.
.
# Chest pain:  Patient has a h/o CAD s/p CABG in ___ and 
presented with ___ substernal chest pain with associated N/V, 
SOB and HA.  Patient received NTG and morphine in the ED and his 
chest pain resolved.  Patient had three sets of cardiac enzymes 
drawn which were at baseline (0.10).  His ECG on admission 
showed TWI in I and AVL, peaked T waves, and ST depressions in 
V5 and V6 compared to prior.  The patient was found to have a K+ 
of 6.7 and was emergently dialyzed in the ED.  After dialysis, 
the patient's chest pain resolved and his ECG returned to 
baseline.  The patient was monitored on telemetry and he was 
placed back on his outpatient regimen of Aspirin, NTG prn, 
Metoprolol, Plavix, and Atorvastatin.  He did not have any 
further acute events during this hospital admission. 
. 
#. Bradycardia:  The patient had AV block upon presentation to 
EMS.  He has a history of bradycardia in the presence of 
hyperkalemia.  The patient was dialyzed in the ED and his 
bradycardia and hyperkalemia resolved.  He was monitored on 
telemetry, and he remained in normal sinus rhythm for the 
remainder of his hospital stay.   
.
#. Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus:  The patient has a history of diet 
controlled diabetes.  On admission, he was found to have a FSBG 
of 360.  He was placed on an insulin sliding scale and his 
glucose was checked every 4 hours.  He did not have any acute 
events during this hospital stay, and he was discharged with 
close outpatient follow-up.   
.
#. End-Stage Renal Disease:  Patient has end-stage renal disease 
secondary to Diabetes, and he receives dialysis on ___, 
and ___.  The patient had emergent dialysis on admission in the 
setting of hyperkalemia.  He was then dialyzed again on ___ 
per his outpatient schedule.  The patient was maintained on his 
home regimen of Nephrocaps and Sevelamer during his stay.  
.
